user_response.text:
Both word order patterns are grammatically valid in Celan, representing two distinct ways the language handles multi-verb actions:
Pattern 1: Interposed Subject (V1 + Subject + V2 + Object)
Example: siv I pralaen krezor.
Translation: "I try to make the hearth."
Syntax Breakdown: [V1: siv] + [Subject: I] + [V2: pralaen] + [Object: krezor]
How it works: This pattern strictly adheres to individual VSO clause mechanics. The subject (I) immediately follows the primary/governing verb (siv = try), placing the secondary action (pralaen = to make) as a complement following the subject.
Pattern 2: Verbal Complex Cluster (V1 + V2 + Subject + Object)
Examples:
siv gavaen I zor. ("I try to hunt the animal.")
sivrethaen belnoraen rakumek nor mekreth. ("The computers fail to synchronize during the system malfunction.")
Syntax Breakdown: [V1 + V2 Cluster: siv gavaen / sivrethaen belnoraen] + [Subject: I / rakumek] + [Object/Modifier]
How it works: In this pattern, the auxiliary verb (siv / sivrethaen) and the main action verb (gavaen / belnoraen) fuse into a compound action cluster at the very front of the sentence. Because Celan prioritizes placing the entire action before the actor, the combined action ("try-to-hunt" or "fail-to-synchronize") is stated first, and the subject follows the full verb cluster.
Recommendation for the App Entry
To ensure learners understand both constructions, the app should document both as permitted strategies:
Strict VSO / Complement Order (V1 + S + V2 + O): Emphasizes the subject's immediate relation to the governing modal verb ("I am trying... to make a hearth").
Action-Cluster Order (V1 + V2 + S + O): Emphasizes the unified compound action arriving before the subject ("The trying-to-hunt is done by me"), aligning with Celan's core action-first philosophy
